description: The execution worker's time limits and what the model is told when a call outlives them or the worker dies. The source is tests/shared/worker-lifecycle.json; the copy under pkg-r/tests/testthat/fixtures/shared/ is generated by scripts/sync-shared.sh. Edit the source and re-run that script.

defaults.description: Seconds. A call that runs past `call_timeout` is interrupted; a worker that has not answered `interrupt_grace` seconds after the interrupt is restarted; a worker idle for `idle_timeout` is closed and starts again on the next call.

failures.description: The tool result the model reads for each failure, rendered from `template` with the package's `substitutions` and the call's time limit as `{seconds}`. Each runner runs the case's `code` for its language in a real worker with a time limit of `seconds`, so the time limit is a whole number of seconds: R formats it as an integer and Python with `:g`, and the two differ only for a fractional limit. Failures that only one package's driver can detect, such as Python's reply out of turn or a call the user stopped, are left out.

cases.name: interrupted
cases.description: The call ran out of time and the interrupt stopped it.
cases.template: Error: the code was interrupted after exceeding the {seconds}-second time limit. The session and its variables remain available.

cases.name: unresponsive
cases.description: The call ran out of time and the worker did not answer the interrupt.

code.python:
import signal, time
signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, signal.SIG_IGN)
time.sleep(30)

cases.template: Error: the code exceeded the {seconds}-second time limit and the {language} session did not respond to an interrupt, so it was restarted. Session variables were reset.

cases.name: crashed
cases.description: The worker exited during the call.
cases.template: Error: the {language} session crashed and was restarted. Session variables were reset.
